_comment_family: Proxima Nova ships as a family, and the two cuts this app carries -
this Black and the Bold beside it - both write 'Proxima Nova' into
name ID 16 with the cut in the subfamily. Asking for 'Proxima Nova'
alone would be a request either of them could answer, and on the one
channel set in both it is the request that decides whether a picked
word is a picked word at all: block and highlight would resolve to
the same file and the highlight would draw nothing.
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way
syne-regular and the two Telegraf packs declare theirs.
The Windows family (name ID 1) is a third spelling again - this file
says 'Proxima Nova Bl' and the Bold says 'Proxima Nova Rg' - because
the family was cut into four-style groups for a font menu that only
ever held four. Neither of those is declared or listed below. 'Rg' in
particular is the REGULAR group's name, so a machine answering to it
would be as likely to hand back a 400 as the 700 that asked.
Weight 900, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Asking for 800 or for 'bold' would invite a browser to
synthesise weight on top of a face that already has all of it.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes.
Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file,
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The PostScript name first, then the Windows full name. Both name this
one cut rather than the family or the four-style group it was filed
in, so a machine answering to either is answering with this file -
which is exactly what the fallback route is for.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, never a design choice - a block laid out against
the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely different, which is
what fontguard exists to catch before anything is drawn.
Written as one half of a pair all the same. Every channel that uses
this face uses proxima-nova-bold with it, the whole of the difference
between them is weight, and the two stacks are written to keep a
weight difference standing when neither file loads. This one falls to
Arial Black, the heaviest face a Windows machine can be relied on to
have; the Bold falls to Segoe UI Semibold, which is lighter than it
and is not a face this stack can reach.
Which of the two is the block and which is the picked word is the
CHANNEL's rather than this pack's. All seven that carry the pair now
answer it the same way - the Bold is the block and this Black is what
a picked word climbs to - and the seven were turned together, from a
block in this cut that stepped down. The fallback pair would hold
either way, because what it preserves is the gap and not a
direction.
Impact sits behind Arial Black rather than in front of it, which is
the other way round from every display pack in this folder. Impact is
condensed and Proxima Nova Black is not: a caption that fell to it
would re-wrap at a width nothing measured, where Arial Black is the
same kind of object as this face at roughly the same set width.
